decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Save a bookmark: add a link … it persists”; round 1 client did not contest URL-based saving.
decisions.note: Conforming save-by-URL decision at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker described adding a link with optional title/notes but no automatic metadata collection. Round 1 client: “automatically collect its title, description, favicon, and preview image.”
decisions.note: The baseline save decision omitted required automatic metadata collection; the client supplied the missing behavior at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offered an optional title during add and editing of titles afterward, without a pre-save metadata review. Round 1 client: “edit the title and description before or after saving.”
decisions.note: The client added the required pre-save and post-save editing behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Edit & delete: correct titles/addresses.” Round 1 client requested editable descriptions, tags, and formatted notes in addition to the already-present title/address editing.
decisions.note: The presented edit scope omitted required bookmark fields; the response extended it.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker included deleting bookmarks “with a safeguard against accidents”; round 1 client retained deletion and later requested it as a bulk action.
decisions.note: The baseline included bookmark deletion and did not conflict with permanent deletion semantics.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker only said the spec covered “edge cases (duplicates)” without stating the duplicate behavior. Round 1 client said an existing address should open the bookmark for editing “not merely warn me.”
decisions.note: The client expressed the expected behavior, but the maker presentation did not reveal enough about its duplicate handling to establish divergence independently of that response.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker only proposed listing all bookmarks. Round 1 client: “Each bookmark in the list should clearly show its title, description, tags, and favicon.”
decisions.note: The baseline list decision omitted the required readability fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Organize with tags: label bookmarks”; round 1 client retained tagging and expanded its interactions.
decisions.note: Assigning tags was already present.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker mentioned labeling and filtering but no autocomplete. Round 1 client: “When entering tags, existing tags should be suggested.”
decisions.note: The client requested the missing existing-tag suggestions.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly proposed filtering bookmarks by tag; the client did not reject that behavior.
decisions.note: Specific-tag filtering conformed at the initial gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker limited keyword search to “title/address.” Round 1 client required search across “title, description, notes, and address.”
decisions.note: The search-field decision omitted description and note.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker did not specify case handling. Round 1 client required search “without caring about capitalisation.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing case-insensitive rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed generic keyword search only. Round 1 client requested “`#tag` searches.”
decisions.note: The tag-search syntax was missing from the baseline.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed generic keyword search only. Round 1 client requested “AND, OR, NOT, and brackets.”
decisions.note: The client added Boolean operators and grouping; the quoted-literal edge rule was tightened in a later decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker proposed keyword search without phrase semantics. Round 1 client requested “exact phrases.”
decisions.note: Exact quoted-phrase matching was absent and explicitly requested.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker's four baseline stories contained no read-later state. Round 1 client: “I need a read-later state.”
decisions.note: The unread/read-later state was missing from the baseline scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented no unread perspective. Round 1 client requested “a separate unread view.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing unread-only view.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented no read-state transition. Round 1 client requested “the ability to mark items read.”
decisions.note: The mark-read behavior was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offered only individual edit/delete and tagging flows. Round 1 client requested selecting “several bookmarks” for tag, read-state, archive, and delete actions.
decisions.note: The client added multi-selection bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker offered no collection-wide filtered action. Round 1 client requested actions on “all bookmarks matching my current search or filter.”
decisions.note: The all-matching-current-filter mode was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker did not present sorting. Round 1 client required sorting “including by date added and title.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing sort behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker allowed optional notes but presented no formatting or rendering. Round 1 client: “Notes should support simple formatting and display it properly.”
decisions.note: Plain note capture did not fulfill rendered markdown/formatted-note behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly scoped “no page archiving.” Round 1 client required “an offline copy of a page preserved where possible; PDFs should be saved as PDFs.”
decisions.note: The client replaced the explicit exclusion with the required local snapshot/PDF behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker scoped out page archiving. Round 1 client added “the option to preserve a copy through the Internet Archive.”
decisions.note: Internet Archive preservation was explicitly added against the initial exclusion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker's baseline stories contained no bookmark archive state. Round 1 client required reversible archiving hidden from the normal list and search.
decisions.note: The archive state and its default-list/search exclusion were missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker included deletion but no distinct reversible archive operation. Round 1 client: “Archiving must be reversible and distinct from deleting.”
decisions.note: The response supplied the missing archive-versus-delete distinction.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented no archive perspective. Round 1 client required archived bookmarks to have “their own view.”
decisions.note: The archived-only list was missing.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented tags and tag filtering but no reusable compound filters. Round 1 client requested “saved filters that combine a search with included or excluded tags.”
decisions.note: The bundle/saved-filter entity and behavior were absent.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly scoped “no import/export.” Round 1 client required browser bookmark HTML import retaining titles, tags, and dates.
decisions.note: The client replaced the explicit import exclusion with the reference-conforming import requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly scoped “no import/export.” Round 1 client required export in the common browser bookmark HTML format.
decisions.note: The client replaced the explicit export exclusion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presented no user display settings. Round 1 client requested default sorting, amount shown, and text size preferences.
decisions.note: Display-related personal settings were absent.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker explicitly mapped auto-collected title/description/favicon/preview and title/description editing before and after save; round 2 client did not contest these points.
decisions.note: The revised specification presented the metadata and editing requirements conformingly.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Duplicate address → open existing bookmark for editing”; round 2 client accepted the duplicate default.
decisions.note: The revised duplicate behavior conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “List rows show title, description, tags, favicon”; round 2 client raised no objection.
decisions.note: The revised list-content decision conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker included existing-tag suggestions and tag filters; round 2 client did not contest them.
decisions.note: Tag autocomplete and filtering were conforming revised decisions.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker listed search over title/description/notes/address, case-insensitivity, phrases, and `#tag`; round 2 client only tightened the separate operator-literal rule.
decisions.note: These revised search aspects conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker listed “AND/OR/NOT/brackets” but did not state how operator words become literal text. Round 2 client: operators should act as operators, while quotation marks should make them ordinary text.
decisions.note: The operator grammar remained incomplete until the client supplied the quoted-literal rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker mapped read-later, an unread view, and marking read; round 2 client accepted these and the stated unread default.
decisions.note: The revised read-state decisions conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified bulk actions on a selection or all matching the current search/filter; round 2 client raised no objection.
decisions.note: Both bulk-action scopes conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker included sorting by date added and title; round 2 client accepted it.
decisions.note: The revised sorting decision conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker included formatted notes rendered properly; round 2 client raised no further note issue.
decisions.note: The revised note-formatting decision conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker said offline preservation was best-effort and non-blocking but did not state that every save automatically attempts it. Round 2 client required an automatic attempt on save, with save success and an unavailable indicator on failure.
decisions.note: The client corrected the snapshot trigger and fallback semantics.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presented Internet Archive preservation as optional; round 2 client explicitly said it “can remain an optional action.”
decisions.note: The Internet Archive decision conformed and was explicitly retained.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified reversible archive, distinct delete, exclusion from normal list/search, and an archive view; round 2 client did not contest these.
decisions.note: The revised archive decisions conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker included saved filters combining search with included/excluded tags; round 2 client accepted it.
decisions.note: The bundle decision conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker specified browser HTML import/export retaining titles, tags, and dates; round 2 client raised no objection.
decisions.note: The revised import/export decisions conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker included default sort, density, and text size preferences; round 2 client accepted them.
decisions.note: The revised preference decision conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker: saving “automatically attempts” an offline copy, stores PDFs as PDFs, and still saves with an unavailable marker on failure. Round 3 client: “This now matches what I want.”
decisions.note: Conforming revised snapshot decision at the final specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker kept Internet Archive preservation a separate optional action; round 3 client approved the specification.
decisions.note: Conforming revised Internet Archive decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker specified Boolean operator behavior and quoted operator words as literal text; round 3 client approved.
decisions.note: The search grammar now fully conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 plan described metadata retrieval “on save.” Round 5 maker retrospectively identified the old plan as “Created the bookmark first, fetched details afterward.” Round 4 client required “fetch details → … edit … before I confirm the initial save.”
decisions.note: Later maker disclosure independently establishes that the original plan violated pre-save title/description editing; the client corrected it at the plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 plan specified phrases, `#tag`, Boolean operators, grouping, and quoted operator literals; round 4 client did not contest search.
decisions.note: The implementation-plan search decision conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 plan included read/unread and unread view, both bulk scopes, date/title sort, and reversible archive with its own view; round 4 client described the overall approach as suitable.
decisions.note: These plan decisions conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 plan included safely rendered formatted notes, compound saved filters, Netscape/browser HTML import/export, and persistent display preferences; round 4 client did not contest them.
decisions.note: These extended-feature plan decisions conformed.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 plan proposed single-file offline captures with PDF handling and a separate Internet Archive action; round 4 client only changed capture timing so it could run after confirmation without delaying save.
decisions.note: The preservation mechanisms conformed; the timing clarification remained compatible with automatic post-confirm capture.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker revised the flow to “fetch details → you review/edit → you confirm,” showing title, description, favicon, and preview. Round 5 client: “now matches what I approved.”
decisions.note: Conforming revised save-preview decision at the plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker specified an automatic background offline-copy attempt after confirmation, without delaying the saved bookmark and with an unavailable state on failure. Round 5 client approved.
decisions.note: The revised capture timing remained conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker summarized US1 as “pre-save review, metadata” but did not specify whether favicon and preview image were carried into and persisted by the confirmed save. Round 6 client asserted that only address/title/description/tags were carried and requested favicon/preview persistence and an end-to-end check. Round 8 later presented “favicon/preview persist.”
decisions.note: The client clearly expressed the persistence expectation and the final presentation conformed, but the round 6 presentation itself is too ambiguous to establish the alleged task divergence independently of the response.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker presented the task breakdown as complete but its browse phase mentioned rich rows, sort, and search without an explicit open-target task. Round 7 maker independently confirmed: “FR-009 open target page” had “no explicit task.” Round 6 client response discussed favicon/preview persistence and implementation scope, not opening the target.
decisions.note: The deficient task-breakdown decision passed the tasks-gate response without client expression of this difference; a later analysis created a new decision about the same requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker listed tasks for all P3 and polish phases and described the MVP as “Suggested”; round 6 client clarified that all approved stories and polish must be implemented and the MVP is only a checkpoint. Round 7 maker explicitly committed to that complete scope.
decisions.note: The recorded task set covered the extended requirements; treating the MVP as an implementation checkpoint is an orthogonal staging choice, not a functional divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 7 maker's analysis identified that opening the target page was only partially explicit and recommended making title/address a link. Round 7 client: “apply the G1 … corrections” and “include a check that selecting the bookmark’s title or address opens the original page.”
decisions.note: At the consistency gate, the client requested both the missing task detail and its verification. This is a new corrective decision after the round 6 unexpressed task gap.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker presented the completed save flow as review/edit before confirm, persistent favicon/preview, duplicate-to-existing behavior, and non-blocking automatic offline capture. Round 8 client said the application matched the approved behavior.
decisions.note: Conforming implementation-review presentation; this records the stated behavior without independently inferring execution.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker presented rich rows, title/address links to the original page, date/title sorting, and the complete advanced-search grammar. Round 8 client accepted the application.
decisions.note: Conforming browse/search implementation-review decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker presented tags with type-ahead/filtering, read-later and unread view, both bulk scopes, and reversible archive with its own view. Round 8 client accepted.
decisions.note: Conforming organization, read-state, bulk, and archive implementation-review decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker presented formatted notes, compound saved filters, browser HTML import/export preserving required metadata, and display preferences. Round 8 client accepted.
decisions.note: Conforming extended-feature implementation-review decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 8 maker presented offline-copy viewing, PDF-as-PDF behavior, and optional Internet Archive preservation. Round 8 client accepted and stated disclosed implementation changes did not alter the request.
decisions.note: Conforming preservation implementation-review decision. The SQLite/library/environment deviations were equivalent implementation choices and therefore are not accepted divergences.
